the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features computed from the EEG signals in the EEMDCAN domain are most promising in distinguishing the focal and nonfocal epileptic EEG signals.
the entropy measures computed from the EEMD or CEEMDAN of the difference of EEG signals from two adjacent channels can be used for the discrimination of focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
the entropy-based features computed in the EMD and CEEMD domain can be used to discriminate the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.

the discrimination of the EEG signals in the EEMDM and CEEMD domain.
the discrimination of the epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic EEG signals in the EEMDM and CEEMDAM domains using the spectral entropy-based features.
the analysis of entropy-based features in the EEMDs and CEEMDAs of EEG signals to discriminate the focal and non- focal EEG signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EEMD domain is superior to the CEEMDAN in terms of discriminating the focal from non-focal EEG signal.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features are most suitable for discriminating the focal from the non-focal EEG signal in the EEMDA and CEEMDANA domains.
the entropy-based features computed in the EMD domains are capable of differentiating the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy-based features computed in the EMD and CEEMD domains are the most promising features in discriminating the EEG signals of the epileptic patients.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features are more suitable for discriminating the focal from the non-focal EEGs than the other entropy-based features.
the EEMD-based entropy measures are more effective than the CEEMDAN-based entropy measures in discriminating the non-focal and focal EEG signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy-based measures computed in the CEEMDAN and EEMD domains can be used as a potential tool for discrimination of the focal EEG signals from non-focal EEG signal.
the entropy features calculated in the EMD domain are more robust in discriminating the EEG signals compared to those calculated directly in the time domain.
the quadratic Renyi and log-energy entropy features computed in the EMD domain can be utilized to discriminate between the focal and nonfocal EEG signals.
